experiment: E1 light cone of one integer
setup: Two bonded worlds identical except the single pair's registry number, replaced through bond.stream=[n]. Variants: control (stream = the world's own number), coin-flip (upper half flipped, lower half kept within 1 unit), agreement-flip (coin kept, lower half moved across the agreement threshold), both symmetric (both ends ask in the step from tick 3 to 4) and asymmetric (Bob's plus detector at DISTANCE+2 so Bob asks in the step from tick 5 to 6).

prediction.before_first_ask: diff empty at every tick <= t_ask (t_ask = the world tick read by the asking step, 3 for a detector at 3 links)
prediction.cone: at snapshot tick t every differing Node lies within Manhattan distance t - t_ask_end of the asking Node for at least one end whose ask has happened; global quantities (escaped totals) may differ only after a ray could have reached the open boundary from the asking Node
prediction.first_differing_tick: t_ask + 1 for the earliest end whose answer changed

pass: no differing Node outside the union of the forward cones, no difference before the first ask, control diff empty
fail: any difference outside the cones or before the first ask, or a nonempty control diff
highlights_sections: 3.18 no hidden nonlocal physics (the registry answer must not give any Node access to remote state beyond the cone)
3.20 a recorded outcome does not rewrite the past (no difference before the first ask)
5.4 ordinary propagation is deterministic; only the Detector encounter draws
note: Highlights section references added after the predictions were fixed; no prediction changed.
